With a single RSU, monostatic sensing mainly reveals the radial component of vehicle velocity, which limits beam prediction on curved roads and at high speed. We combine monostatic and bistatic observations from distributed RSUs using standard OFDM waveforms, without dedicated sensing waveforms or extra signaling. Results show more accurate beam prediction and higher achievable rates than single-RSU and learning-based baselines, with the largest gains under high mobility and on curved roads.
